info.title: Tiger SMS Public API
info.description:
Single dispatcher transport: `GET|POST /stubs/handler_api.php?action=<name>&api_key=<key>&...`. All parameters (GET or POST) are read the same way — send them as the query string either way.

Auth: `api_key` query parameter, a 32-character alphanumeric token from your account. Missing/invalid key → plain-text `BAD_KEY`, HTTP 401, before any action code runs (checked by shared middleware for every action below).

Unknown `action`, or any unexpected server error inside a known action → plain-text `BAD_ACTION`, HTTP 200 (dispatcher never lets an exception escape as a 5xx).

Currency is USD-only across every new response: ISO numeric `840`, no RUB, no converters. Money values are 4-decimal HALF_UP internally; fields that are historically strings in this API family stay strings (trailing zeros trimmed where the source formatter does so — see per-field notes).

New behaviour ships behind `api_*` Setting flags, default OFF. While a flag is OFF, that action/parameter/error behaves exactly as if it did not exist (existing actions: byte-identical old response; brand-new actions: plain-text `BAD_ACTION`, HTTP 200, same as any unrecognized action). Flags referenced below are informational — this document describes the TARGET behaviour once a flag is flipped ON.

Rate limiting for the heaviest read/write actions (`getNumber`, `getNumberImsi`, `getNumberV2`, `getPricesV3`) is enforced both in the application and, for actions covered by the edge configuration, before PHP. An edge 429 is always plain-text `Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header, regardless of the JSON-envelope flag.

Provider purchase/cost price and real vendor names are never exposed by any action in this document — only the public numeric `provider_id` and SALE price ever appear (getProviders, getPricesV3).

Comma-separated lists (our differentiator vs. competitors): `providerIds`/`exceptProviderIds` on the getNumber family accept them unconditionally (pre-existing). Top-level `service`/`country` accept them only on the price-lookup methods (getPrices, getFreePrices, getPricesV2, getPricesV3) and only under flag `api_prices_comma_list_enabled` — see each method's parameters for the exact flag.

The api_key in every example/parameter default in this document is the placeholder `YOUR_API_KEY` — it never contains a real key.

Gated by flag `api_active_activations_enabled` (currently ON in this environment). While OFF, this action returns plain-text `BAD_ACTION`, HTTP 200, byte-identical to an unknown action.

get.summary: Purchase a phone number for a service/country.
get.description:
Purchase a phone number for a service/country.

Accepted but currently ignored (no validation rule, silently dropped, no error): operator, phoneException, minPrice.

Automatic country detection (e.g. `country=any`) is not supported: `country` must be a numeric country code — a non-numeric or unknown country returns BAD_COUNTRY.

Comma-separated lists on this method are supported for providerIds/exceptProviderIds only. Top-level `service`/`country` do not accept comma lists here — that capability is coming soon on the price-lookup methods (getPrices/getFreePrices/getPricesV2/getPricesV3) only.

getNumberTest behaves exactly like getNumber, but is the documented way to explicitly pass activationType/testParams.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Fixed for this operation.

parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: Your account API key. Placeholder shown — never a real key.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: sms_activate-style service code.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Numeric country code (sms_activate_code).

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description: Require a variation that allows multiple SMS to the same number.

parameters.name: maxPrice
parameters.description: Ceiling price in USD, 4dp. <=0/non-numeric is treated as "not set" (default sellable ceiling), never as "unlimited".

parameters.name: providerIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated provider ids to restrict the purchase to (our differentiator, pre-existing). Pick ids from getPricesV3/getProviders for the same pair: pricing follows those providers' price buckets, and maxPrice is validated against their cheapest bucket. multiple=1 purchases are charged a fixed price equal to the cheapest qualifying bucket of the selected providers.

parameters.name: exceptProviderIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated provider ids to exclude.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Referral id, falls back to the `ref` cookie.

parameters.name: activationType
parameters.description: One of SMS, CALL_FLASH, CALL_VOICE, CALL_INTERACTIVE, RENT_SMS. Unknown value silently falls back to SMS. RENT_SMS is accepted but rental is not a supported product yet — do not rely on it.

parameters.name: fixedPrice
parameters.description: Literal 'true'/'false'. Requires maxPrice. When 'true', the charge is locked to exactly maxPrice instead of the usual hold-then-settle-at-real-price flow. [flag: api_fixed_price_enabled]
